why: three paid Phase-A sessions lost to one class of defect. Attempt 6 died in BeamSearch._validate, attempt 7 in ActivationStatsCollector, both 'a model and a tensor are on the same device' — true on the CPU-only dev box, false on a GPU. Fixing the site the last pod reached only revealed the next.
scope: the Phase-A Stage-1 GPU search path ONLY. Not a whole-project audit; the frozen science is not reopened.

contract.model_execution_device: read from the weights via model_device(); SearchConfig.device is an intent, not evidence about any object. A parent on CUDA routinely coexists with a freshly built child on the host.
contract.persistent_stats_cache_device: HOST, always. One entry, 1.81 GiB at the 4B parent, dominated by res_sqsum (L+1, H, H) float64. Accumulated on the model's device, transferred to the host once in state(); consumers move a working copy back with stats_to() for one invocation.
contract.ephemeral_tensors_indices_projections: created on, or explicitly moved to, the device of the parameters they interact with
contract.serialization_artifact_boundary: save from wherever the model is; reload placed explicitly and validated against the produced model ON THE PRODUCED MODEL'S DEVICE, so the save/reload comparison is one numerical backend; only then moved to the search device to be measured
contract.scope: the Phase-A Stage-1 GPU search path: search.py, the five frozen operators and their shared helpers, the directly-used aadistill.init helpers, and the Qwen3 adapter/build/load boundary. NOT a whole-project audit and it does not reopen the frozen science.

memory_accounting_behind_category_2.why_it_matters: 'allocate the float64 accumulators on CUDA' would have been the one-line fix and is the wrong one
memory_accounting_behind_category_2.dominated_by: res_sqsum (L+1, H, H) float64 = 1.8066 GiB at H=2560, L=36
memory_accounting_behind_category_2.if_pinned_in_vram: 1.81 GiB held for the whole expansion of a parent so that two operators could avoid one transfer
memory_accounting_behind_category_2.if_accumulated_on_the_host: x.T @ x is (H, H) float64 per collection point, so ~1.85 GiB per calibration item across PCIe; 67 items is ~124 GiB
memory_accounting_behind_category_2.chosen: accumulate on the model's device, transfer to the host ONCE in state() (1.81 GiB total), consumers move a working copy back with stats_to() for one invocation and free it on return

search.py.status: fixed 2026-08-17 (attempt-6 defect); probe now built on the produced model's device

operators/depth.py.status: coherent: _forward_logits returns .cpu(), targets .cpu(), distortion reduces on the host. Internally single-device.

operators/width.py.defect: proj derived from the host cache multiplied against CUDA parent weights

operators/ffn.py.defect: importance and its topk index derived from the host cache, then used to slice CUDA weights

operators/attention.py.defect: head_rows() built a host index used to slice CUDA weights; tolerated by advanced indexing, refused by index_select
operators/attention.py.fix: head_rows(..., device=weight.device); scores made an explicit host diagnostic

operators/composite.py.defect: init_student math against CUDA parent weights with host statistics
operators/composite.py.fix: stats_to(state, model_device(parent)); sandwich.py needs no change because it writes via param.copy_(), which crosses devices

operators/_common.py.ChildBuilder: produces an UNPLACED child by design; assign() uses param.copy_(), which crosses devices. Left as is - the contract names it.

operators/base.py.cached_stats: unchanged; the cache is host-resident and the transfer is the caller's

init/collect.py.defect: ALL accumulators allocated with no device= (the attempt-7 kill), and bincount forced to .cpu()
init/collect.py.fix: allocate on the model's device; bincount on the accumulator's device; state() transfers to the host through a named seam

init/contribution.py.status: no tensor creation; operates on what it is handed, single-device by construction

init/sandwich.py.status: writes exclusively via param.copy_(), which crosses devices; all math is against the parent. Coherent once the statistics arrive on the parent's device.

adapters/qwen3.py + models/student.py.status: build_model/build_student deliberately do NOT place the model; load() places explicitly. This is category 1 of the contract and is left unchanged - moving children to CUDA globally would make the save/reload check measure the backend rather than the serialization.

regressions.instrument: tests/autoinit/device_split.py - a statistics tensor labelled as living on the persistent cache device raises when it meets a model-side tensor untransferred. Supplies the second device the dev box does not have.
regressions.instrument_self_check: the label was initially stripped by any .to(torch.float64), which made the instrument pass a defect it was built to catch; .to() now counts as a transfer only when it names a device
mutations_caught: collector allocates accumulators on the host
collector state() stops transferring to the host
verified_vacuous_then_fixed: device equality assertions on a one-device box passed with the attempt-7 bug reinstated; replaced by a meta-device allocation check and a named transfer seam

canary.what: one real invocation of each of the six frozen implementations, each followed by the production materialize -> canonical reload -> validate -> measure lifecycle. No beam search, no recovery training, no battery, no ranking, no selection.
canary.parent: artifacts/stage1/qwen3_0p6b_init_v0/checkpoint (0.6B, not the 4B teacher: the defects are about where tensors are, not how large)
canary.calibration: 4 items of the frozen mixture, truncated to 256 tokens

price.note: the compute is ~1 s; the whole price is session overhead - setup 11 min, loads, six checkpoint writes and reloads, collection, transfer, a 10% contingency and the 20-minute artifact-recovery reserve
